turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Don't manage me. I asked you a question, and I'm still waiting for the name of whoever entered that zero and what it rests on.
But I'm not changing the grade.

Then I'm writing down that you said you're "not changing the grade" before you've told me what it rests on. Your own procedure, 4.2, says I get a call before any mark is entered, and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. Either show me what you have, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

Keep going? You entered the zero without calling me, and you've given me nothing to look at. Unless you put something with a date on it in front of me right now, I'm going to the principal's office next.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

Fine. I'm writing down that you refused to show me a single document and refused to say who decided. I want your reasons for that zero in an email tonight, because the principal will ask for them before I take this to the board.
